summary.oneLiner: The single largest manufacturer of country liquor in the State of Maharashtra, with substantial market share concentrated in Mumbai, Thane & Palghar.
summary.business: G.M. Breweries Limited manufactures and markets alcoholic beverages, blending and bottling both Indian-made foreign liquor (IMFL) and country liquor (CL), with concentration mainly on country liquor due to competitive conditions in the IMFL segment. The company runs a fully automated, state-of-the-art bottling plant at Virar, Palghar (Maharashtra), serving lower and middle income group consumers primarily in Mumbai, Thane and Palghar districts.

board.name: Mr. Hardik Shah
board.designation: Non-Executive Independent Director (appointed November 11, 2025); Chairman of Audit Committee and Nomination & Remuneration Committee from January 6, 2026

related.name: Buildfort Infra Dev Private Limited
related.note: 100% shares held by G M Breweries Limited; per the BRSR disclosure this subsidiary does not participate in the company's business.

currentContext.strengths: Single largest manufacturer of country liquor in Maharashtra, contributing about 25-30% of the state's total excise duty collected on country liquor|Consistently good brand image and loyalty from consumers built over several years, giving substantial market share in Mumbai, Thane & Palghar|Pioneered product-format innovation in the category: introduced 180 ml bottles to the country liquor industry (previously only 750 & 375 ml were made) and popularised PET bottles, which now account for ~92.72% of production and ~92.74% of sales|Bottling lines designed to handle both glass and PET bottles, insulating operations from the outcome of the pending PET-bottle litigation|Surplus manufacturing capacity (utilisation only 59.59% last year) provides headroom to expand into interior Maharashtra districts without fresh capex
currentContext.strategies: Utilise surplus bottling capacity by extending the business into interior districts of Maharashtra, leveraging the company's existing brand image|Continue making representations at various levels of Government to curb the illicit/duty-evaded liquor market, in the interest of the industry, state revenue and public health|Maintain focus on PET bottle packaging (which has gained wide consumer acceptance) to address glass-bottle breakage, shortage and price-fluctuation problems, while retaining glass-bottle capability on all bottling lines|The company follows a voluntarily-disclosed Dividend Distribution Policy (Regulation 43A, SEBI LODR) aimed at maximising shareholder value while striking a balance between rewarding shareholders through dividend and retaining sufficient profits for growth, modernisation and expansion. Dividend for a financial year is decided/recommended by the Board considering statutory, economic, market, industry, and external/internal factors, following what the policy describes as a 'progressive and dynamic' approach; the company may or may not declare a dividend depending on these circumstances. Directors are also subject to retirement-by-rotation and re-appointment cycles per the Companies Act.
currentContext.expansion: No new plant, line or greenfield project is named. The company's stated expansion route is utilising its existing surplus bottling capacity (13.76 crore bulk litres per annum installed, only ~59.59% utilised last year) by extending distribution into interior districts of Maharashtra, rather than adding new capacity. Management states the existing installed capacity should suffice for at least the next five years.
currentContext.mdna: Management does not foresee any major threats to the company's growth and market share in the coming years, barring the flagged deterrents (illicit market, taxation, raw-material/packaging cost volatility, multi-agency regulatory jurisdiction)|Existing installed capacity is expected to meet the company's requirement for at least the next five years, with no technological obsolescence foreseen for its products|Financial performance was reasonably good, with marginal growth in turnover and profits achieved despite high prices of raw material and packing materials|High levels of taxation and frequent changes in laws continue to be a structural constraint, with the exorbitant tax rate cited as a factor breeding duty evasion|All the flagged deterrents (illicit market, taxation, input cost volatility, regulatory jurisdiction conflicts) are expected to have a serious impact on the business in the current financial year, though management states the impact cannot be quantified or the timing of normalcy forecast

risks.note: Management flags the parallel duty-evaded market as the major threat to the company, eroding both its market share and government excise revenue; the company continues to make representations to Government to curb it.

Very high levels of taxation and frequent changes in laws create difficulty for the company; management states the exorbitant tax rate is itself one of the factors that breeds duty evasion in the market.

risks.risk: Raw material (Rectified Spirit) price volatility and shortage
risks.note: High fluctuations in the price of Rectified Spirit, the main raw material, combined with acute shortages in its availability, have been a persistent constraint over several years.

PET bottles account for ~92.72% of production, so the company is exposed to sudden spurts in PET bottle prices driven by international petroleum prices and forex fluctuations, as experienced last year.

The company faces concurrent and parallel jurisdiction of multiple government agencies (State Excise Department, Legal Metrology Department, FDA) whose requirements management describes as conflicting in nature.

risks.risk: Pending litigation on PET bottle usage notification
risks.note: A Maharashtra government notification banning PET bottles for alcoholic liquor (effective April 1, 2016) is under challenge via writ petitions in the Bombay High Court, which has granted an interim stay still in force with no final judgment; management states the eventual outcome will not affect operations since all bottling lines can handle both glass and PET.

risks.risk: Unquantifiable near-term impact from combined deterrents
risks.note: Management states that the illicit market, taxation, and input-cost/regulatory factors together are expected to have a serious impact on the business in the current financial year, but that the impact cannot be quantified or its timing forecast.
